questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: What was the main stated goal of the First Crusade (1096-1099)?
options: To capture Jerusalem and the Holy Land from Muslim control
To conquer Rome for the Pope
To colonise North Africa for trade
To convert the Vikings to Christianity
questions.answer: To capture Jerusalem and the Holy Land from Muslim control
questions.why: The First Crusade was launched by Pope Urban II in 1095 to reclaim Jerusalem and other holy sites for Christendom. A common mix-up is confusing Crusade goals with unrelated conquests like Rome or Viking conversion.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: What is generally given as the date of the fall of the Western Roman Empire?
questions.why: 476 CE is the year the last Western Roman emperor, Romulus Augustulus, was deposed. Students often confuse this with 1453 (fall of Constantinople/Eastern Empire) or 1066 (Norman Conquest), which are much later events.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: In the feudal system, what did a vassal typically owe their lord in exchange for land?
options: Money rent paid in gold coins only
A share of all crops to the king directly
questions.why: Feudalism was based on an exchange: lords granted land (fiefs) to vassals, who in return owed military service and loyalty. A common misconception is thinking it worked like modern rent or taxation.

questions.subject: English
questions.why: Romeo and Juliet was written by William Shakespeare around 1595. Marlowe and Chaucer are other famous English writers but from different periods, and Dickens wrote much later, in the Victorian era.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: What poetic form does Shakespeare use for the famous Prologue that opens Romeo and Juliet?
questions.why: The Prologue is a 14-line sonnet with rhyming iambic pentameter, summarising the plot. Students sometimes confuse Shakespeare's structured sonnet form with looser forms like free verse.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Which quote best reflects the theme of love vs hate in Romeo and Juliet?
options: 'My only love sprung from my only hate'
'Wisely and slow; they stumble that run fast'
questions.answer: 'My only love sprung from my only hate'
questions.why: Juliet's line directly captures the play's central tension: her love for Romeo is tangled with the deadly feud between their families. The other quotes touch on related ideas but don't state the love/hate paradox directly.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: In a science experiment testing how temperature affects plant growth, what is the dependent variable?
questions.why: The dependent variable is what you measure as an outcome — here, plant growth. The temperature is the independent variable (what you change), and pot type/water are controlled variables that must stay constant. A common error is mixing up which variable is 'caused' vs 'measured'.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Which group organised and led the First Crusade?
options: European Christian knights and nobles, called by the Pope
Muslim leaders seeking to expand territory
questions.answer: European Christian knights and nobles, called by the Pope
questions.why: Pope Urban II called for the First Crusade in 1095, and it was carried out by European knights and nobles. Students sometimes wrongly credit the Byzantine Emperor as the leader, when he only requested help.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: What best describes the shift in political power after the fall of Rome in Western Europe?
options: Power became fragmented among local lords instead of one central empire
A single new emperor immediately replaced the Roman emperor
Democracy spread quickly across former Roman lands
The Catholic Church took over all political power instantly
questions.answer: Power became fragmented among local lords instead of one central empire
questions.why: After Rome's fall, there was no strong central authority, so power split among local lords and kingdoms — this fragmentation is a root cause of feudalism. A common misconception is imagining a smooth, immediate transition to a new single ruler.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: In what city and country is Romeo and Juliet primarily set?
questions.why: Romeo and Juliet is set in Verona, Italy, home to the feuding Montague and Capulet families. Students sometimes assume it's set in England since Shakespeare was English, but he set many plays abroad.
